description: Two shifts (255 min + 330 min) in one Monday-start workweek at 283c/h. Cumulative rounding per stream gives per-shift regular wages 1203 and 1556 and a week total of 2759, not the 2760 that per-shift rounding produces.
notes: Plan Design 1, Worked example A, and .pr1-spec.md row W1. Units are 1/6000 cent; regular numerator = rate * minutes * 100; roundCents(x) = (2x + 6000) / 12000 with integer division. Both shifts fall in the Monday-start workweek beginning Mon 2026-09-28 (Mon 09-28 and Tue 09-29), total 585 min < 2400 threshold, so every minute is regular and the overtime stream is empty. Shift A (255 min = 4.25h): 283 * 255 * 100 = 7216500 (= 1202.75c). Cumulative after A = 7216500; roundCents = (14433000 + 6000) / 12000 = 14439000 / 12000 = 1203 (1203.25 truncated). A = 1203 - 0 = 1203. Shift B (330 min = 5.5h): 283 * 330 * 100 = 9339000 (= 1556.50c). Cumulative after B = 7216500 + 9339000 = 16555500; roundCents = (33111000 + 6000) / 12000 = 33117000 / 12000 = 2759 (2759.75 truncated). B = 2759 - 1203 = 1556. Week = 1203 + 1556 = 2759 = roundCents(16555500), the exact sum 1202.75 + 1556.50 = 2759.25 rounded half-up. Each shift is within 1c of its naive rounding (1203 vs 1202.75; 1556 vs 1556.50). Wrong answers: today's per-shift path rounds B alone to 1557 (1556.50 half-up) and sums 1203 + 1557 = 2760; the plan says the golden fixture expects 2759 and roundsPerShiftNotPerTotal is superseded. Order within the week is workDay then period rank, so A (Mon) is allocated before B (Tue). Tips are all zero so earnedIncome == wages. Policies start Mon 2026-01-05 with confirmed provenance so no value is marked assumed and completeness is .complete.
